newsitem.title: JAPAN: CURLING-PLAY-BY-PLAY COMMENTARY TESTED FOR OLYMPICS.
newsitem.headline: CURLING-PLAY-BY-PLAY COMMENTARY TESTED FOR OLYMPICS.

text.p: Curling spectators at next year's Nagano Olympics will get a play-by-play commentary on radio earphones if a trial run at the world junior championships proves successful, Olympic organisers said on Wednesday.
In a first for the sport, two curling experts will provide in-house commentary in Japanese at the junior worlds, which begin on Saturday in Karuizawa, 90 kms south-east of Nagano.
"If it works well, then we'd like to include it in the Olympics," said chief organiser Makoto Kobayashi.
With up to five matches held simultaneously, public announcements are restricted at major events to avoid disturbing the competitors.
But the long silent matches, which can last up to three hours, can prove tedious.
The tiny radios will cost spectators 500 yen (about $5).
"With a lot of other sports, you get an immediate impact of what's going on, whereas in curling it's not as easy to understand," said Kobayashi.
